options.text: A factor that speeds up photosynthesis
A factor that only affects respiration
A factor that is always present in excess
A factor that is in shortest supply and prevents the rate of photosynthesis from increasing further

questions.explanation: A limiting factor is the factor in shortest supply that prevents the rate of photosynthesis from increasing any further, even if other factors are increased.

questions.stem: On a bright sunny day with warm temperatures, which factor is most likely to be limiting photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: On a bright, warm day, light and temperature are not limiting. Carbon dioxide concentration (only about 0.04% of the atmosphere) is most likely to be the limiting factor.

questions.stem: How do commercial greenhouses use knowledge of limiting factors?

options.text: By controlling light, temperature, and CO2 levels to maximise crop yields
By keeping plants in the dark

questions.explanation: Greenhouses can provide artificial lighting, heating, and supplementary CO2 to ensure no factor limits photosynthesis, maximising the growth rate and yield of crops.

questions.stem: On a graph of rate of photosynthesis vs light intensity, what does the plateau (flat part) indicate?

options.text: Light is no longer the limiting factor; another factor is now limiting

questions.explanation: When the graph levels off, increasing light intensity no longer increases the rate. This means another factor (usually CO2 or temperature) has become the limiting factor.

questions.stem: Why is CO2 enrichment used in some greenhouses?

options.text: To increase the rate of photosynthesis beyond what normal atmospheric CO2 levels would allow

questions.explanation: Atmospheric CO2 is only about 0.04%, which often limits photosynthesis. Increasing CO2 levels to around 0.1% in greenhouses can significantly boost the rate of photosynthesis and crop yields.

questions.stem: At night, which factor limits photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: At night there is no light, so light intensity is the limiting factor for photosynthesis. Without light energy, photosynthesis cannot occur regardless of other factor levels.

options.text: The point where the rate of photosynthesis equals the rate of respiration
The point where all factors are at their maximum
The point where all CO2 is used up

questions.explanation: The compensation point is the light intensity at which the rate of photosynthesis exactly equals the rate of respiration, so there is no net gas exchange.
